notes.title: Rattus Velocitas update released.
notes.notes:
[p]G'day Rat Racers. [/p][p][/p][p]This patch adds some way overdue updates to the scoreboard and makes the game a lot more predictable on certain older AMD graphics systems, in addition to other bugfixes and optimisations. [/p][list][*][p]Made the Race Results scoreboard only show Rats that have finished their race if it's still running when all Human players finish.[/p][/*][*][p]The Race Results scoreboard now shows finish times for every participant! :)[/p][/*][*][p]The game now calculates the finishing position at the end of the race based on the race time, rather than the order players touched the finish line trigger.[/p][/*][*][p]Significantly improved determinism of gameplay actions and physics. [b]NOTE: This will desync existing replays, due to the physics behaving slightly differently![/b][/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a long-standing bug where item throwing trajectories in replays were off by 1 frame, causing some item throwing trajectories to fail to reproduce correctly. [b]NOTE: This bugfix only reliably fixes replay files recorded with this patch onward. Older ones may be fixed too but it is not guaranteed.[/b][/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a bug causing the starting and looping parts of background music to desync on lower end CPUs.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a bug where the fadeout to the Race itself from the loading screen would happen instantly on lower end CPUs.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a startup crash on older AMD Adrenalin graphics drivers on Windows if the Steam Overlay was enabled [b]and[/b] the computer had just been started up. [/p][/*][*][p]Fixed the game hanging when loading a race on some systems.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a bug where the game's first tutorial prompt wouldn't appear on first game launch.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a bug where setting an Antialiasing setting higher than 2x MSAA on some AMD graphics systems would crash instantly and prevent the game launching again. 
[b]NOTE: This bugfix may increase VRAM usage. Please make sure your graphics card has 1GB of video memory or more for optimal performance.[/b][/p][/*][*][p]Significantly optimised rendering performance. [/p][/*][*][p]Temporarily removed the "Unrestricted" option from the FPS cap dropdown - this setting was causing stability issues on some AMD graphics systems. (again) [/p][/*][*][p]Workaround a bug where the game would erroneously show as running in Steam after game shutdown if the Game Manual was opened during the game session with certain PDF viewers. [b]NOTE: This means for now that a file browser window will open instead in the game data directory where the Game Manual is located. I will have a better solution in a later game update.[/b][/p][/*][/list][p]Known issues:[/p][list][*][p]Some combinations of graphics settings and AMD graphics cards on Windows may cause the game to repeatedly crash on startup; if this happens to you, try deleting %userprofile%/AppData/LocalLow/Hedgehog Arts/Rattus Velocitas/settings/settings.json and relaunching the game. 
Settings to avoid in particular on Adrenalin driver 22.6.1 (which is the last supported driver on a [b]lot [/b]of AMD hardware and is the primary culprit of all crashes on the Vulkan renderer) are MSAA, Vsync and Frame Blending. [b]If your graphics card is of RDNA1 generation or newer, please try updating your AMD drivers instead![/b][/p][/*][*][p]The flashing lights in Space Station flash in sync rather than at random times. This will be fixed in a future patch.[/p][/*][*][p]On some systems, alt-tab will sometimes crash the game. Again, if you're on AMD hardware and have an RDNA1 generation graphics card or newer, try updating your drivers if this happens to you.[/p][/*][*][p]Sometimes sounds from despawned Missiles will linger in splitscreen multiplayer after despawning.[/p][/*][/list]

notes.title: A message regarding AMD graphics cards on Windows.
notes.notes: [p]G'day Rat Racers.[/p][p]In the past month I have been receiving increasing reports of AMD graphics cards on Windows struggling to run this game, with some computers outright crashing on startup. If this is happening to you, as of today, I have added an extra launch configuration that launches this game using D3D11 instead of Vulkan, which seems to be the root cause. [/p][p]In the event you can't see the new launch configuration and want to try D3D11 mode on an AMD graphics card:[/p][list][*][p]Right-click Rattus Velocitas > Properties[/p][/*][*][p]In the Steam Launch Options, enter -force-d3d11[/p][/*][*][p]Close the properties box, then launch the game.[/p][/*][/list][p]Please note that the "Reduce Latency" option in D3D11 mode may result in a significant framerate reduction, this is a known issue.[/p][p][/p][p]UPDATE 7th September 2025: I have also identified an issue where the same AMD systems can sometimes hang when loading a race. For this specific case, please use -disable-async-load in your launch options to workaround the problem.[/p][p]I have now fixed both of these bugs and will ship fixes for them in the game update coming this Tuesday 8am AEST.[/p]

notes.title: Weekly report
notes.notes:
[p]G'day Rat Racers, and welcome to the weekly report! [/p][p]This one is a little late as I've been spending a lot of time making the game's upcoming online mode work, and work smoothly! This was also why last week didn't have a weekly report, as I was doing a lot of planning for how to tackle the online implementation.[/p][p]For starters, it will be peer to peer. If your computer's internet connection cannot properly obtain direct connections to other players, a relay server will manage this situation for you![/p][p]The new network lobby system coming along with the LAN and Online update will also reflect this, displaying a warning if a player (or your PC) couldn't achieve a direct connection to your machine for whatever reason. (Pictured, this particular test was simulated)[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45629180/3c8db6c4a0f633dff8bc55b2f83413d3ab11e145.png"][/img]In addition, the current planned menu flow is as follows:[/p][list][*][p]As usual, you'll choose "Join Rat Race," however a [b]new[/b] menu with the options "Local" and "LAN/Online" will appear. [/p][/*][*][p]Selecting the "LAN/Online" option will bring you to a screen, where you'll typically pick "Go Online," then "Enter Matchmaking." Matchmaking is completely random and will match you with the first lobby with open player slots and no race running, otherwise it will create a new one.[/p][/*][*][p]After a 30 second countdown, all players will be thrown into a race akin to picking "Quick Race," only it's just yourself vs the others in the lobby. First to finish the race wins and can add another win to their stats. ;)[/p][/*][/list][p][b]In addition, the Matchmaking Server software will be made available for anyone to use, for free. 
[/b]More details on how this will work will be revealed closer to the launch of Online mode.[/p][p]This will allow anyone to run their own matchmaking server. The game will also have a private lobby option available at launch which will, instead of queuing everyone into a Quick Race, allow the player at the top of the lobby player list to pick the Race Course Environment or even enter a custom Track Seed, just like in singleplayer and splitscreen![/p][p]And that's this week wrapped up. Happy Rat Racing! This concludes this weekly report. [/p]

notes.title: Weekly report
notes.notes:
[p]G'day Rat Racers, and welcome to the weekly report! [/p][p]Things have been a little slow since the last update dropped, so I'd like to use this weekly report to reflect on why races in the game are only one lap and future plans for multi-lap race courses. [/p][p]If all you want to know is about the future online mode, feel free to skip to the bottom of the report. Without further ado...[/p][p]You may or may not be already asking; why [i]does [/i]this game only have a single lap per race? The answer is actually a rather old codepath in the game. Enter the game's [i]original[/i] method of procedurally generating race courses:[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45629180/79a52e5eaf28ebcdf1f2135b33fe0530db7598fa.png"][/img]As you can see, this was wildly different to the current game build; tracks were generated using 5 types of segments, with the segments going all the way up into the sky to avoid overlapping each other. These tracks were one continuous road as a result which meant the game could only realistically support one lap.[/p][p]This legacy system however wasn't working for the Volcanic region very well and didn't work for Beach at all; the original concept for Volcanic called for racing [i]inside[/i] the volcano through an archway in the side rather than around the edge of the top and this system struggled to keep the track segments from clipping into the Volcano's sides. Beach was self-explanatory; I've never seen a shoreline rise out of the water like these tracks did! I did attempt to allow track segment overlap but this made the track layout incredibly confusing to traverse if it got too long.[/p][p]To solve all of these issues and some playability issues with the old procgen, I rebuilt the track generation to use splines instead, with mesh extrusion and some rather confusing math doing a lot of the heavy lifting to turn a cyclic spline into a race course. Pictured below is Desert from the release version of Rattus Velocitas:[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45629180/5e1320153fd3c39c2c762d873357f230646edb11.png"][/img][/p][p]This allowed both Volcanic and Beach to actually work well as race courses vs the old approach, but another possibility arose with the introduction of cyclic tracks; multiple laps. In a future update, I'm planning on giving race courses a truly random length, with said length deciding the lap count as an additional layer of track variety![/p][p]Finally, a pretty common question from the very small audience of this game; "where's the online mode?"[/p][p][b]And I can finally announce that it's being worked on! Lobbies already work but a lot more work is required before the game's able to run online races correctly.[/b] In addition, I will be taking a unique approach to online play's accessibility that will allow proper game preservation, if ever someone wanted to preserve this game. More about that and other aspects of online play's implementation in a future weekly report.[/p][p]And that's this week wrapped up. 
Happy Rat Racing![/p]

notes.notes: [p]G'day Rat Racers.[/p][p][/p][p]This update contains visual bugfixes and an updated game manual:[/p][list][*][p]Fixed a visual bug where particle effects on Rats' hover bikes in the Main menu were misaligned[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed Players 2-4's Rats' hover bikes having no particle effects at all.[/p][/*][*][p]Updated the Game Manual:[/p][list][*][p]Updated the "How to start a Splitscreen Race" section of the manual to describe the new player join system.[/p][/*][*][p]Updated the Troubleshooting section to add one new issue and remove a now-resolved known problem with Splitscreen multiplayer.[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list]

notes.title: Rattus Velocitas update released.
notes.notes:
[p]A new Rattus Velocitas update has been released!
More about this update's content can be found in the weekly report released in conjunction with this update.[/p][p][i]NOTE: Due to a rather stupid mistake on my side with tracking first place finishes, your save file's progress will be reset when you first launch this update. I do apologise for the inconvenience, fortunately this won't happen again. Your selected Rat Skin will not be affected. More details are in this patch's accompanying weekly report.[/i][/p][p][i]NOTE: This update will partially break replays that had a ??? item attempt to target a player already over the finish line. This is only a visual bug and won't appear in new replays.[/i][/p][p][i]NOTE: The game manual currently still references the old Splitscreen multiplayer systems, this will be rectified in a future update.[/i][/p][list][*][p][b]Added the first wave of Steam Achievements![/b] Enjoy attempting to obtain these. Additionally, just racing normally will likely unlock a lot of them.[/p][/*][*][p]To avoid confusing new players, the Player Profile menu is now accessed via a separate button in the Main Menu, rather than the Steam profile tile in the top-left.[/p][/*][*][p]The game now only needs 5 races to achieve Rat Racing Apprentice (down from 10)[/p][/*][*][p]The game now makes it obvious if onboarding is in progress, with the remaining races required to complete onboarding; this notification appears on the left side of the "Join Rat Race" menu.[/p][/*][*][p]The game now displays a notification to tell the player the performance ratio calibration has completed. This information is accessible via the player profile menu.[/p][/*][*][p]Splitscreen multiplayer has been partially overhauled:[/p][list][*][p]Now, instead of selecting how many players will play a race, players are now required to press START or the equivalent button to "join" their controller to the play session. The player controller icons on the bottom of the screen reflect this. Physically disconnecting a controller or turning it off will automatically remove a player.[/p][/*][*][p]Due to this overhaul, it is no longer possible to change input device from KBM to Gamepad and vice versa during gameplay. Additionally, all controllers need to be disconnected to change back to Keyboard input while inside the Main Menu. [/p][/*][*][p]Player controllers no longer rearrange themselves after the race finishes if a controller got disconnected then reconnected during gameplay.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]The player number select screen in the Main menu has been replaced with a Race Start confirmation:[/p][list][*][p]Splitscreen participants can now change their Rat colour from the new "Ready to Race?" screen that replaces the old "How many players?" screen.[/p][/*][*][p]In addition, in singleplayer, this screen gives Player 1 the ability to change their Rat fur colour without entering the Player Profile menu first.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Added Bronze, Silver and Gold Rat colours obtainable by ranking up as you play more races; look out for them! [/p][list][*][p]The Bronze skin is awarded for Rat Racing Conoisseurs, the Silver skin for Rat Racing Champions and the Gold Skin for Rat Racing Legends.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Fur shading on Rats has been improved.[/p][/*][*][p]Shading on Rats' eyes have been improved slightly.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a bug where audio volumes on startup were quieter than intended if not at 100% until the Options Menu's audio controls were adjusted and/or the game was paused then unpaused again.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a bug where background music didn't loop properly on the first loop.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a bug where world shadows sometimes didn't render properly at specific track sizes.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where the publisher logos would stutter badly if the graphics driver was updated and/or the game was launched for the first time on a new computer. The game now properly waits for this process to finish.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a regression with the previous update's CPU-side optimisations that completely broke audio in splitscreen multiplayer for other viewports. [/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a bug introduced by the previous update that caused Player 4's audio in 4-player splitscreen to be distorted.[/p][/*][*][p]Tweaked the volume levelling and balance for 4-player splitscreen's speaker allocation to sound close to singleplayer's volume in most circumstances; please provide feedback if you play this mode often![/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an oversight that caused Dialog windows (example: Rat Racing Rank notifications) to have extra buttons that didn't actually do anything useful. [/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where ??? items would disappear completely while in flight if near the finish line. [/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a bug where the Replay List would stop working after viewing a replay then exiting it via the pause menu until a normal race was played.[/p][/*][/list][p]Known issues:[/p][list][*][p]In splitscreen multiplayer, some distant vehicles at high velocities are sometimes louder than intended.[/p][/*][*][p]Sometimes spent Missiles in splitscreen games leave behind a persistent Missile flight sound in the game world.[/p][/*][/list]

notes.title: Weekly report.
notes.notes:
[p]G'day Rat Racers, and welcome to the weekly report! [/p][p]Today I'll be discussing the newest update's upcoming content, which will be released in a few hours at most. [/p][p]The first thing I would like to talk about is game progress; While implementing the Steam Achievements coming with this update, I discovered that the game was [i]not[/i] tracking first place finishes. For any race. At all. Oops.[/p][p]I immediately corrected this when I found it but what about existing save files? Technically this means somehow a player may have done 100+ races but had [b]none[/b] of them count as first place finishes, which would make certain achievements very difficult if not borderline impossible to achieve for existing "broken" saves.[/p][p]Now we're left with a difficult decision; either keep existing save files as-is and risk some achievements being harder to get for some players, or have each save file soft-reset from scratch. Another idea I had was to reset only the race counts but grandfather in the old racing rank. Unfortunately this didn't work as well as I'd hoped in practice as admittedly the game's code is a bit of a spaghetti mess.[/p][p]Therefore I've regrettably had to go the nuclear option; With the next game update, all race progress on your save will be reset. I do apologise for this insane slip-up and will ensure save file breaking changes don't happen in future. [/p][p]Your currently selected Rat Skin will be kept however and the game will pretend you've first launched the game exactly on the day this upcoming update is installed and launched, which will allow certain achievements to unlock correctly. Your performance ratio will also be reset to 50/50 (new saves start at 60/40) and recalibrated; more on changes to this in the coming sections of this report.[/p][p]Now, onto the new content. There is now an [i]entirely[/i] [i]new[/i] Splitscreen system! This new interface completely replaces the old "How many players?" screen.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45629180/1fe06648dd70c71f3df419b41f60f842d1416551.png"][/img]Players now join and leave by connecting a controller and pressing their controllers equivalent of the Start Button (START on an Xbox Controller, OPTIONS on a PlayStation(R) Controller) and leaving by physically/wirelessly disconnecting their controller. In addition, multiple Rats now appear on this screen, one per player, where you can visibly see which Rat colour you've chosen. [/p][p]As you can see, each player can now select their own colour, instead of inheriting Player 1's colour. Colour changes to Players 2-4 are temporary and will reset when the game is closed - let me know if you'd like this to be permanent.[/p][p]Speaking of permanent, once a race has started, controller order is [i]finally [/i]preserved across races.
Yes, even if someone's controller's batteries die mid-race and have to be changed or that Bluetooth dongle from Temu couldn't keep up with having all three of your friend's controllers connected. [/p][p]Now, a sneak peek at the Rat Racing Rank rewards; the game now rewards Bronze, Silver and Gold Rats to players who complete specific numbers of races! When a new rank is unlocked, as per the previous game update, the game will show a notification but this time it will also unlock one of these new colours. (Click on the images to view at full size)[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45629180/0edd98c35a4f6768af58b51524ef1b1d28735607.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45629180/6d4dc93048ade9f6ec7945fe7836f7c7517f9bcb.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45629180/8f8770c66049808092fa778ab8a57821b2903458.png"][/img][/p][p]Speaking of race progress, I have altered the OOTB (That is, Out-of-the-box) experience of the game a bit, given recent feedback. Admittedly, it was hard to tell for some players if the game's numerous modes in "Join Rat Race" actually existed in the game or not until the first milestone (completing 10 races) was hit. In addition, the player profile tile in the top left of the main menu didn't exactly make itself obvious as a selectable button to enter the Player Profile menu. I have addressed this with the following:[/p][list][*][p]Now when first booting the game, any time you select "Join Rat Race," a box will appear on the left side showing the game is in "onboarding" mode, along with the number of races remaining to unlock all other race modes. [/p][/*][*][p]The game now only requires 5 races to achieve "Rat Racing Apprentice," which unlocks all other race modes [i]and[/i] Hard CPU difficulty. This also means new players will have raced through each race environment type [i]once [/i]before unlocking this milestone, and can immediately have fun with the other race modes.[/p][/*][*][p]The player profile menu is no longer accessed via the top-left profile tile; it now has it's own separate menu button, positioned between the "Watch Replay" and "Options" buttons.[/p][/*][*][p]Because the game's performance ratio calculation needs 7 races worth of data before the rolling average can operate correctly, a separate notification now appears if you re-enter the main menu after your save records the 7th completed race. [/p][/*][/list][p]And that just about covers everything. Along with this new content are plenty of bugfixes too, namely for splitscreen audio as I accidentally broke that in a previous patch without realising. (oops) Happy Rat Racing, and I'll see you all next week in the next Weekly Report![/p]

notes.title: Weekly report.
notes.notes: [p]G'day Rat Racers![/p][p][/p][p]This is the start of a Weekly Report post I'll be making each week, either before or after the release of a game update. Expect more of these in future![/p][p][/p][p]One thing I've felt was lacking in the game's progression system since release was the absence of any unlockable rewards for hitting specific milestones, such as ranking up in your player profile. The first way I'll address this is something some of you may have been waiting for; Steam Achievements. I'm glad to announce that they're now in the pipeline!  [/p][p][/p][p]Several of the progression achievements already work in an internal test build, and more will be added in future updates. In addition, there will be three new Rats unlockable with the rankup system! Bronze, Silver and Gold rats will be unlocked by achieving Rat Racing Connoisseur, Rat Racing Champion and Rat Racing Legend as you play. [/p][p][/p][p]Now, let's talk about Splitscreen. While the Splitscreen multiplayer [i]works[/i], there were several issues I identified with it when I finally had the chance to test it properly with 4 players:[/p][list][*][p]If someone's controller disconnected, they'd be able to reconnect it and keep playing, but the controller order would then rearrange itself after the race ends.  [i]The testing scenario for this was rather extreme as we were playing on a TV wirelessly streaming the host PC's screen, with all four controllers connected via a Bluetooth Adapter behind a wall. Definitely not the best setup to play on if you care about latency but it did uncover this issue so it had a silver lining![/i][/p][/*][*][p]Currently, every splitscreen player's rat fur colour is the same as the Player's chosen colour for splitscreen races. This is undesirable both because of player visibility and also the fact your friends can't pick their favourite colour. :( [/p][/*][/list][p]I'll be addressing both with a new "player join" system that requires a player on a different controller to press a button to be joined up to the game session, rather than having any player select the number of participants after selecting the game mode, race course environment and CPU difficulty. The aim is to keep the original controller order even if a player drops out and reconnects. In addition, the screen that will replace the original "how many players?" menu will be where your friends (and yourself, for that matter) can pick their favourite colour to race with. [/p][p][/p][p]And finally... A previous update broke the audio for player 4 and muted some audio cues for players other than player 1. Oops. This has already been fixed internally and will ship with the next game update.[/p][p][/p][p]And that is all!  [/p][p]This update was originally intended to ship this week but it's been deferred as it needs a little more time to cook. See y'all again in the next weekly report. [/p]

notes.title: Rattus Velocitas update released.
notes.notes:
G'day Rat Racers.

This is a small patch that fixes the following issues:
- Cheese when dropped while being consumed didn't have a deterministic trajectory in replays.
- Fireballs in Volcanic didn't have a deterministic path in Replays.

notes.title: A small performance adjustment update.
notes.notes: For rat racers playing from lower end hardware, I've included a fix for dynamic resolution not scaling when it should with specific framerate targets.

notes.title: Wednesday bug bash update.
notes.notes:
G'day Rat Racers!
Here is a set of bug fixes and game adjustments to improve the gameplay experience.

[list]
[*] Item balance has been adjusted: 
- Boost obtained from consuming Cheese dropped by another player reduced from 64ms to 16ms
- Portable Dash Ring drop chance increased from 18% to 19%
- ??? Item drop chance decreased from 2% to 1%
- ??? Item no longer randomly explodes in circumstances where it has otherwise no reason to self-destruct. 
[*] Missiles now warn the player they're locked on to with an "INCOMING" crosshair.
[*] Being baited by the Cheese Item now causes slowed sparks to appear on the player's vehicle.
[*] Reworked the Collision Detection for the Cheese item when dropped. This fixes the following issues:
- Sometimes collisions with dropped Cheese in Replays didn't replay correctly.
- When already eating a piece of Cheese, players were briefly blocked by dropped Cheese on the road.
[*] Improved CPU artificial intelligence in cases where targeting an Item Container's more favourable than targeting a Dash Ring.
[*] Optimised CPU and memory garbage collection performance of Item Containers and their visual effects.
[*] Optimised CPU and memory garbage collection performance of Mini Volcanoes' fireballs in Volcanic.
[*] Optimised CPU and memory garbage collection performance of Coconuts present in Beach.
[*] Optimised CPU and memory garbage collection performance for ALL Explosion effects.
[*] Optimised CPU and memory garbage collection performance of Bombs, Cheese and Shields. 
[*] Introduced asynchronous race loading; if this causes hangs, please launch the game with "-disable-async-load" in your Steam launch options.
[*] Fixed a hang on AMD graphics cards running Radeon Software 22.6.1 when loading into a race or back into the menus.
[*] Fixed a rare crash on NVIDIA graphics cards when loading into a race or back into the menus.
[*] Fixed a rare hang on NVIDIA graphics cards when loading into a race or back into the menus.
[*] Changed certain physics interactions to be more deterministic; now Replays should reproduce close to exactly the same as the original match it was recorded from, as well as making bomb bounces more predictable.
[*] Fixed a bug that allowed players to cancel gravity while in freefall by using certain items.
[*] Fixed a bug where thrown away items (in Item Containers) that hadn't yet landed on the ground could physically block players.
[*] Fixed a bug that made it possible to throw away items while eating.
[*] Fixed an edge case with Missiles at their maximum flight speed where it was possible for them to miss a target going around a corner while also going round said corner themselves.
[*] Fixed Replays showing the incorrect estimated race time. Older replay files will show --'--"--- instead.
[*] Fixed a case where it was possible to fail to finish a race in Forest if the player finishing was too far to the sides of the finish line when crossing it.
[/list]
[b]Note that older Replay files will break in various ways this patch: Missiles will no longer replay correctly and the Cheese may function erratically in old replay files. Additionally, old replay files will also display 00'00"000 for their EST time as it wasn't originally stored in the replay data. [/b]

notes.title: Another bugfix patch.
notes.notes:
[list]
[*]Fixed a regression introduced by the gamepad freeze fix; now Rumble on compatible controllers should work again.
[/list]

notes.title: New Rattus Velocitas patch released.
notes.notes:
[list]
[*]Fixed a bug that caused the game to hang if using a wireless PlayStation(R) controller with rumble enabled. (NOTE: Rumble still requires connecting said PlayStation(R) Controller via USB)
[b]This resolves the known issue where having controllers connected wirelessly with rumble enabled freezes the game; the workarounds are not needed anymore.[/b]
[*]Fixed a bug where toggling the reduce buffering setting didn't reload the graphics settings automatically.
[*]Made reduce buffering off the default setting for new installations; on systems that only meet the minimum GPU specifications, this setting may cause stuttering so it's recommended to keep this setting off there. 
[*]Fixed Missile targeting sometimes skipping targets when fired with a viable target directly in front of you.
[*]Improved visibility of the road in Forest by lining extra rocks along the sides.
[*]Updated the Game Manual's Troubleshooting section to reflect this patch's changes.
[/list]

[b]Please note this patch breaks replay files made in previous versions, due to the missile targeting changes.[/b]

notes.title: Day 0 bugfixes released.
notes.notes:
- Fixed an issue where the Performance Ratio could swing wildly in one direction after a streak of failing to beat the EST time then a race where you did beat it. This was rather prominent on fresh saves, now fresh saves should have a more stable performance ratio. Saves from the release build of this game will eventually correct themselves as well.
- Fixed an issue where the wrong slash character ('/' instead of '\') was used when displaying the Performance Ratio in the Player Profile
- Adjusted the audio mix of the Ghost Missile (??? item) explosion to make it more distinguishable from a Shield shattering.
- Fixed a bug where dropped Cheese didn't properly disable it's glow effect when picked up.

notes.title: Rattus Velocitas has been released!
notes.notes: [p]G'day, rat racers![/p][p][/p][p]The game is now out! Thank you for trying it out and have fun! [/p][p]Now, for issues I'm aware of that could make it difficult to run and/or may impact gameplay.
